Subject: On‑prem MAP kickoff — deployment owners, VPN & KMS alignment

Alicia / Horizon team —

Thanks for choosing Redwood for this private deployment evaluation. To get the MAP moving quickly I want to align owners and immediate asks so we can lock a 6‑week evaluation cadence and map the close timeline. Suggested internal owners (happy to adjust):

- Networking / VPN lead: Mateo Alvarez (networking engineer)
- IAM / KMS lead: Karthik Iyer (security & infra)
- Deployment topology & sizing: Marissa Cole (prod infra)
- Technical PM / CS coordinator: Dev Patel

Immediate asks for kickoff meeting:
1) Horizon POC list (networking, security, procurement) — names + emails
2) Confirm if you will use customer‑managed KMS (AWS KMS CMK) or a vendor‑managed key
3) VPN type preference (IPSec site‑to‑site / AWS Transit / Direct Connect) and any firewall egress rules we should know about
4) Any compliance checkpoints up front (SOC2 artifact, specific encryption policies)

I attached a draft MAP workbook and a simple network diagram to review ahead of our call. Proposed timeline: week 1 kickoff + config, week 2–3 test harness + eval, week 4 pilot traffic, week 5 validation, week 6 signoff. If that works, we’ll schedule a 60‑minute kickoff next week.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555‑0148

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem MAP kickoff — deployment owners, VPN & KMS alignment

Alicia / Hannah —

Thanks — brief technical notes from the infra/security side so Horizon can prep:

- KMS: yes, Redwood supports customer‑managed AWS KMS keys (CMKs). We will need an IAM role with a trust policy allowing our deployment account to assume the role. Required KMS permissions: kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:DescribeKey on the CMK. We can provide a template policy and a minimal trust role during kickoff.

- HSM / BYOK: for customers who require an HSM we also support PKCS#11 integration via a partner appliance; that will be a separate engagement if needed.

- VPN: IPSec site‑to‑site is straightforward. Please confirm: public IP for your VPN gateway, preferred IKE version (v1/v2), and whether you have a static CIDR we should route. We will need the following egress ports open: 443 (TLS for control plane), UDP 500/4500 for IPSec, and the usual ephemeral ports for the management channel.

- Data flows & topology: for the MAP trial we typically run a small dedicated VPC with strict routing to your VPN plus a test subnet for evaluation traffic. Marissa can share a sizing estimate once we know expected TPS and token rate.

Action items for kickoff:
1) Horizon to share CMK ARN + IAM contact
2) Horizon networking to share VPN public IP and NAT/firewall egress rules
3) Redwood to provide role & KMS policy templates, and a bootstrapped network diagram update based on Horizon inputs

Happy to jump on the call to walk through the templates.

—
Karthik Iyer
Staff SRE (Security & Infra) | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
